title: Acting on design feedback
idea: Iteration is turning review comments into small, tested design changes, and a good design makes most of those changes local to one class.
points: Log every comment as a bug, missing requirement, or preference.
Bugs and missing requirements mean fix now; preferences mean discuss or known trade-off.
Change one class at a time and rerun your tests after each change.
If one comment forces edits in many classes, revisit that boundary.

edges.label: listen
edges.caption: Write each comment down as said. Do not defend or fix during the review.

edges.label: classify
edges.caption: Label each comment a bug, a missing requirement, or a preference. The first two are c05-t08's fix now.

edges.label: pick one
edges.caption: Take the most important fix-now item. Preferences go to discuss or a known trade-off.

edges.label: verify
edges.caption: Rerun the tests. A green run means nothing else broke.

edges.label: next round
edges.caption: Show the updated design and start the next round with fresh eyes.

code.title: A comment becomes a class
code.caption: Times are hours as numbers, so 0.25 is 15 minutes.

walk.text: The base class is the interface; `StrictOverlapPolicy` is the rule you presented.
The reviewer's request becomes `BufferPolicy`, the gap rule from c05-t03. No existing class is edited.
`BookingRepository` holds the bookings, so the service keeps no list of its own.
`BookingService` passes the room's bookings to whichever policy it was given.
Same bookings, two policies: back-to-back meetings pass one rule and fail the other.

takeaway: Log, triage, change one class, rerun tests, present again.

starters: What if I disagree with a reviewer's comment?
How do I tell a design bug from a style preference?
When is a change too big to make before submission?
